featured.title: Go Home to Apply — The Rule That Could Force 118,000 Indian Green Card Seekers Out of America
featured.excerpt: A new USCIS memo guts adjustment of status, the pathway 69 per cent of employment-based immigrants have used to become permanent residents without leaving the country. For Indians stuck in decade-long backlogs, leaving may mean never coming back.
featured.image_caption: A US permanent resident card, commonly known as a green card
featured.nri_angle: Indian nationals dominate the employment-based green card queue and face the longest backlogs in the system — often 10 to 30 years for EB-2 and EB-3. Forcing them to leave the US for consular processing means abandoning jobs, pulling children from schools, and gambling that a consulate in India will process their case before their employer moves on. For the roughly 862,000 Indians in the green card queue, adjustment of status was never a shortcut — it was the only way to maintain a life while waiting.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India Gave Foreign Funds a Tax Holiday on Government Bonds. It Forgot About Its Own Diaspora.

technology.title: Banks Are the Only Vertical Keeping Indian IT Alive. The FY26 Numbers Prove It.
technology.excerpt: BFSI now accounts for nearly a third of revenue at TCS, Infosys, and HCL — and it is the only segment growing while tech, telecom, and retail shrink.
technology.image_caption: Candlestick chart showing a downward trend in stock market analysis
technology.nri_angle: Over a million Indian IT workers — many on H-1B and L-1 visas in the US — are employed by these companies. Heavy BFSI concentration means a banking downturn would ripple through India's largest white-collar workforce.

technology.title: Satya Nadella's Build Week Went Sideways. The Stakes Have Never Been Higher.
technology.excerpt: A leaked 'addiction' memo, a training-data scandal, and seven new in-house AI models — Microsoft's most important developer conference in a decade delivered fireworks nobody planned.
technology.image_caption: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella at a company event
technology.nri_angle: Satya Nadella remains the most powerful Indian-origin CEO in global tech. Microsoft employs tens of thousands of Indian engineers on H-1B visas across Redmond, Hyderabad, and Bangalore. Build 2026's push toward in-house AI models and agentic platforms directly shapes the roles — and job security — of this workforce.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Europe Just Built a Firewall Around Its Cloud. Indian IT's Biggest Clients Are on the Other Side.
technology.excerpt: The EU's new Technological Sovereignty Package creates a four-tier classification system for cloud services that could lock out American hyperscalers — and the Indian firms that depend on them.
technology.image_caption: The Berlaymont building in Brussels, headquarters of the European Commission which unveiled the cloud sovereignty proposals (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: Indian IT services giants — TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCL Tech — derive billions in revenue from European clients, largely through AWS, Azure, and GCP partnerships. A sovereignty framework that restricts hyperscaler access to sensitive EU contracts directly threatens this revenue stream and the thousands of Indian tech workers deployed in Europe.

technology.image_caption: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who called Marvell Technology a future trillion-dollar company (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: Indian chip designers are central to the custom silicon revolution powering Marvell, Broadcom, and hyperscaler in-house chip teams. Marvell's design centres in India contribute to the networking and optical interconnect chips driving its AI growth. For NRI investors, the S&P 500 inclusion triggers passive fund inflows that typically lift newly added stocks.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: T-Mobile Is Hiring 1,000 Engineers in Hyderabad. It Just Laid Off Hundreds in America.

technology.nri_angle: The GCC boom validates Indian engineering talent but accelerates offshoring that makes H-1B workers in the US anxious. Indian Americans sit uncomfortably at the intersection — their homeland's gain is sometimes their adopted country's loss.

technology.nri_angle: UPI's international expansion directly affects NRIs — cheaper remittances, seamless travel payments, and a growing India-connected financial ecosystem. The India-UAE CBDC corridor will reshape how NRI money reaches home.

technology.title: A New Bill Wants to Kill the H-1B-to-Green-Card Pipeline. Big Tech Should Be Nervous.
technology.excerpt: The American White-Collar Worker Jobs Act would slash visa duration to two years, eliminate OPT, and end dual intent — a direct strike at the Indian talent pipeline that powers Silicon Valley.
technology.image_caption: The United States Capitol building at dusk in Washington, D.C.
technology.nri_angle: Three-quarters of all H-1B holders are Indian nationals. The bill would upend the life plans of hundreds of thousands of Indian engineers at Google, Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon — and devastate the US business model of Infosys, TCS, and Wipro.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Zuckerberg Says AI Spending Is Forcing Meta to 'Take Down' Its Workforce. His Flagship AI Model Just Stumbled.

technology.nri_angle: Meta employs thousands of Indian engineers across its Bay Area offices — the same offices that absorbed the heaviest cuts. The layoffs hit integrity, cybersecurity, and content design teams disproportionately, roles where Indians are heavily represented.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Perfios Just Hit Unicorn Status. It Proves India's Biggest Fintech Export Isn't an App.

technology.nri_angle: Perfios represents the Indian B2B fintech infrastructure stack becoming a global export — the credit decisioning and compliance rails that banks in Southeast Asia, the Gulf, and Africa are building on.
